newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Volume, volatility jump in IBM.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Volume, volatility jump in IBM.

text.p: Options on shares of International Business Machines Corp were busy Thursday as investors sought protection amid another sharp decline in the underlying shares.
Volatilities in the options rose sharply along with the volume, traders said.
By about 1220 CST/1820 GMT, the computer giant's stock was down 3-5/8 points at 130-1/8 on consolidated volume of 4.15 million shares. The stock reached 128-7/8 in early trading before recovering.

Traders said the stock was hit by renewed concerns about the company's first quarter earnings, touched off by the Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street column, which highlighted recent earnings downgrades by some analysts who follow IBM.

Options traders said rumors were also surfacing that the company may pre-announce a first quarter earnings disappointment, but traders in the underlying stock doubted IBM would pre-announce a shortfall.
One analyst said he spoke to IBM Thursday "and they have no plans for a pre-announcement." IBM declined comment.

Jon Najarian, president of Mercury Trading, the designated primary market maker for IBM options, said the renewed earnings worries were the main factor driving up volume and volatility in the options.
He said volatilities had climbed to the upper 30 region from the upper 20 area Wednesday.

"Last month we'd been averaging a volatility of about 26 percent in IBM," he said. "That was during that whole tech wreck. We didn't get the big jump in volatility that everybody else (in the technology sector) did."
"People are scared, people are looking for protection," he added.
Najarian said investors were getting protection by buying puts directly and by creating synthetic puts through buying calls and selling stock.
The biggest action was in the April 130 put, which traded nearly 4,900 contracts. The July 135 put traded 3,065 contracts and the May 125 put traded nearly 2,900.
Among the calls, the April 135 call traded 3,965 contracts and the April 140 call traded about 3,100.
Najarian said some investors believe IBM shares could drop to 115 if they are unable to hold 130.
Technical analyst Gregory Nie at EVEREN Securities said the stock is in danger of breaking below its 200-day moving average, but a band of support lies in the 123 to 130 zone.
The 200-day moving average was at 132 Thursday afternoon.
"It's another step down, but not critical just yet," he said, referring to the stock's slide.
"Somewhat subjectively, a break under 120 I think is the point where you say you've got a brand new downtrend that's in charge and has superseded the previous uptrend," he said.
